item.title: Domain-uniform integration lower bounds and local information
item.description: arXiv:2611.08524v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study deterministic numerical integration on open subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ of volume one. Let $e_n$ be the minimal worst-case error using at most $n$ function values. For twice continuously differentiable functions with the normalized Lipschitz bounds proposed by Novak, we prove $e_n\geq v_d^{-2/d}n^{-2/d}/(4(d+2))\geq(8\pi\mathrm e)^{-1}n^{-2/d}$, where $v_d$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. This resolves Novak's conjecture: the lower-bound constant is independent of the dimension and the shape of the domain. A midpoint rule on the cube has the same rate, up to an absolute constant. The proof uses smooth functions that vanish near the sample points and are large elsewhere. The bound therefore remains valid when each sample supplies all local information about the function. For scalar linear targets continuous in the uniform norm, we prove a second result on the global smooth class with prescribed function, gradient, and Hessian bounds: adaptive local information has the same minimal error as values and gradients at points chosen in advance. We give extensions to function recovery, finite integration measures, and anisotropic derivative bounds.
item.dc:creator: Yutong Zhang

item.title: Proof of the Cordero-Torregrosa Conjecture and an Improved Order Bound for Paired Jacobian Evaluations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In solving systems of nonlinear equations, one of the main objectives is to construct iterative methods that attain high orders of convergence using as few evaluations as possible. However, the information a method obtains during each iteration imposes limitations on the order it can guarantee. The Cordero--Torregrosa conjecture proposes a bound on this order in terms of the number of evaluations of the function and its Jacobian. In this work, we prove this bound for the universal local order of one iteration, without requiring the number of Jacobian evaluations to be less than or equal to the number of function evaluations. In particular, our result also covers the case in which more evaluations of the Jacobian than of the function are performed. The proof encompasses deterministic, causal, memoryless methods whose rules may be arbitrary, without imposing rationality, continuity, or computability conditions. Moreover, we prove that when each Jacobian evaluation is performed at a point where the value of the function is already known, a more restrictive bound on the order of convergence can be obtained. Finally, we propose a new conjecture that establishes a refined bound through a product of factors determined by the distribution of evaluations, under additional dimensional conditions. These results provide a better understanding of the limitations imposed by the available information and raise new possibilities for studying high-order iterative methods.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Alberto Castro Mar\'in

item.title: Multilevel kernel approximation of log-Euclidean manifold-valued functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.08817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study kernel approximation and multilevel residual correction for functions with values in a manifold that admits a global logarithm onto a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, such as positive definite matrices, exponential Lie groups, and Hadamard manifolds. Approximating in logarithmic coordinates keeps the approximant on the manifold and transfers Hilbert-space error estimates verbatim. To express these errors in the natural geometry of the target, we prove metric comparisons. In particular, we obtain a sharp, scale-invariant bound between the log-Euclidean and affine-invariant distances on positive definite matrices, with a constant that depends only on condition numbers. For multilevel approximation, compactly supported kernels scaled to the fill distance give algebraic convergence with sparse, uniformly well-conditioned systems. These guarantees require appropriate sample locations and approximation scales. Compact groups are treated through a principal logarithm, where a bi-invariant metric gives error bounds with constant one. Finally, the log-Euclidean and Karcher means differ by $\mathcal O(r^3)$ near the identity and by $\mathcal O(r^2)$ around a general point, where $r$ is the logarithmic data radius and the second bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Nir sharon, Holger Wendland

item.title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime $(1-\beta_2)/(1-\beta_1)\ll1$. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow ($Re=100,400$) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Enzhan Zheng, Xiaoliang Song

item.title: On optimal convergence rates for parametrized variational problems with applications to nonlocal models
item.description: arXiv:2611.09011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an abstract variational framework for convergence rates of parametrized problems and their Galerkin approximations, with applications to nonlocal diffusion. The main objective is to quantify modeling and discretization errors in terms of the nonlocal horizon, the mesh size, the Sobolev regularity of the local solution, and the compatibility of boundary data. We establish error estimates in energy and $L^2$ norms and develop an adaptation of the Aubin--Nitsche argument that uses regularity of the limiting local dual problem. This approach yields improved $L^2$ estimates without requiring additional regularity of the nonlocal dual solutions, including for integrable kernels. We apply the framework to two constant-horizon nonlocal Laplacians with exterior boundary data and to heterogeneous localization models with classical Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions. The resulting estimates provide quantitative guarantees of asymptotic compatibility and improve existing error bounds under weaker regularity assumptions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence rates and examine the sharpness of the estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zhaolong Han, James Scott, Xiaochuan Tian

item.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Tianchi Yu, Ivan Oseledets

item.title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.09135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.
item.dc:creator: Ziyi Lei, Houqi Su

item.title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
item.description: arXiv:2611.09137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.
item.dc:creator: Zetao Fei, Josselin Garnier

item.title: A Structured-Surrogate Double-Model Approach to Regularization Parameter Selection
item.description: arXiv:2611.09158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double-model methods select a regularization parameter by matching the discrepancy between two reconstructions of the same data to a prescribed target. The Structured-Surrogate Double-Model (SSDM) framework is developed around a computationally inexpensive structured surrogate of the forward operator and a spectrally explicit perturbation, with the selected parameter subsequently applied to the original inverse problem. Given a prescribed target, parameter selection requires neither prior knowledge of the noise level nor training data. For a class of Tikhonov regularization problems, the squared discrepancy is shown to attain a strict maximum at zero regularization, decay as $\lambda^{-2}$, and decrease strictly beyond an explicit phase-aware threshold. A complementary, data-dependent certificate is established to guarantee strict monotonicity on finite intervals, enabling unique and reliable target matching even when the global threshold is overly conservative. The discrepancy is further connected to directional roughness in image deblurring, providing a geometric interpretation of the selection principle. Experiments on synthetic images and on synthetically blurred natural photographs illustrate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical applicability of certified parameter selection.
item.dc:creator: Malena Espa\~nol, Markus Juvonen, Samuli Siltanen, Ilaria Trombini, Chuyang Wu

item.title: A structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method for variable-density incompressible flow with a partitioned time integrator
item.description: arXiv:2611.09171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preserving density bounds and mass conservation, together with a conservative momentum discretization and exact incompressibility, is a central challenge in high-order simulations of variable-density incompressible flow. We develop a structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method that couples conservative density transport with an \(H(\mathrm{div})\)-conforming mixed discretization of the momentum equation. The method uses a partitioned time integrator: density is advanced explicitly by strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta stages with a bound-preserving limiter, while momentum is updated by a linearly implicit backward differentiation formula. The transport velocities are extrapolated from previously computed mixed velocities. Because the discrete solenoidal space is linear, this extrapolation preserves elementwise zero divergence and single-valued normal traces, providing compatible transport velocities without an auxiliary reconstruction or projection. For source-free transport on triangular meshes with impermeable or periodic boundaries, we prove bounds for density cell averages and limiter control-point values under the stated spatial, quadrature, and stagewise Courant--Friedrichs--Lewy conditions. The conservative fluxes and mean-preserving limiter yield global mass conservation. Numerical experiments on triangular and structured rectangular meshes demonstrate the expected convergence rates, machine-level divergence errors, and bound preservation, including in a low-density regime with high density ratio.
item.dc:creator: Zonghao Bai, Yinhua Xia, Yan Xu

item.title: Construction of DAE solver Rodas4PW and numerical test examples with Rosenbrock and W-methods in OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl
item.description: arXiv:2611.09174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper compares various Rosenbrock and Rosenbrock W-methods. To achieve this, some methods implemented in the Julia package OrdinaryDiffEqRosenbrock.jl are selected and benchmarked using test examples. The test examples include stiff ODE problems as well as differential-algebraic equations. In addition to the already known methods, the new W-method Rodas4PW is introduced and included in the tests.
item.dc:creator: Gerd Steinebach

item.title: Boundary integral methods and shape reconstruction for periodic fluid--solid interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.09201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies direct scattering by periodic fluid--solid interfaces and interface reconstruction from multifrequency near-field data. Using Helmholtz decomposition and quasi-periodic single-layer potentials, we formulate a coupled boundary integral system with the standard stress traction, establish its equivalence to the original fluid--solid transmission problem under suitable assumptions, and construct a corresponding Nystr\"om discretization. For near-field observations at finitely many measurement points, we establish local Fr\'echet differentiability of the observation map with a quadratic remainder estimate. In the smooth setting, the derivative transmission problem and its boundary integral formulation are used to compute the observation Jacobian required for interface reconstruction. The interface is reconstructed by regularized Gauss--Newton iteration in a Fourier space that is progressively enriched as the frequency increases. Numerical experiments assess direct-solver accuracy and reconstruction performance for different interfaces, material configurations, and noise levels.
item.dc:creator: Yongxin Liu, Junliang Lv, Ning Wang, Yi Wang

item.title: On the convergence of Lattice Boltzmann method for advection-diffusion equation with intermediate scaling
item.description: arXiv:2611.09245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this article is to study the convergence of a lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) for a simple diffusion equation. The LBM is proven to be stable and consistent in some sense, so that convergence results may be obtained. The approach is similar to asymptotic analysis in the literature, although the schemes are also studied for intermediate time scalings. Usually, LBM are used in the range of acoustic regime, where $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x, or in diffusive scaling, with $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x 2 . In this work, we study any intermediate scaling $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x 1+r with r $\in$]0; 1]. The goal is to prove that this scaling is capable of approximating an advection-diffusion equation, provided the relaxation rate is chosen in accordance with $\delta$x. Convergence results are established and match the previously known results in the diffusive regime. The second objective is to prove that several choices for the initial condition are suitable for convergence. In particular, the usual choice of equilibrium distribution at initial time guarantees that the LBM scheme yields an accurate approximation of the macroscopic quantities.
item.dc:creator: Francky Luddens (LMRS)

item.title: A semi-implicit exactly well-balanced relaxation scheme for the 2d shallow water system
item.description: arXiv:2611.09281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a semi-implicit, exactly well-balanced finite volume scheme for the two-dimensional shallow water equations over a non-flat bottom, aimed at the low-Froude-number regime. The method combines a Suliciu-type relaxation of the pressure with a flux splitting that separates the fast acoustic waves from the slow transport ones: the pressure subsystem is integrated implicitly and the transport subsystem explicitly, so that the time step is no longer restricted by the acoustic stability condition. Written in terms of its Riemann invariants, the pressure subsystem decouples into independent one-dimensional problems along the grid lines, each of them governed by a banded linear system whose bandwidth does not depend on the mesh. The implicit step therefore requires no non-linear solver and costs O(NxNy) operations, regardless of the acoustic Courant number. A two-dimensional exactly well-balanced reconstruction, whose limiter weights are frozen within each time step, preserves this linear structure for the second-order scheme. We prove that both the first- and the second-order schemes preserve water-at-rest equilibria exactly, and we assess them on several two-dimensional benchmarks, where they resolve fine-scale velocity structures on coarse meshes and run up to 8.5 times faster than standard explicit Riemann solvers.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ignacio Ram\'irez-Fuentes, Cipriano Escalante, Tom\'as Morales de Luna, Mar\'ia Luz Mu\~noz-Ruiz

item.title: High-order FEEC discretization on 2D and 3D domains with a disk-like coordinate singularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor-product splines mapped from a square to a disk-like domain form a discrete de Rham complex, but at the coordinate singularity the pushed-forward $0$-, $1$- and $2$-forms are discontinuous, unbounded and not square integrable. Existing polar constructions impose either high-order regularity on the $0$-forms only, or first-order regularity on the whole complex. For general disk-like mappings composed with a smooth diffeomorphism, we construct polar subspaces of all three tensor-product spaces that are conforming, form a cochain complex with the cohomology of the disk, and are $\mathcal{C}^{\mathfrak{r}-m}$ at the center for $m$-forms, for any $\mathfrak{r}$ up to the spline degree, under a compatibility condition between the mapping and the angular basis. The construction enriches the $2$-form space with projected polynomials and lifts them to curl-like $1$-forms by Poincar\'e-type homotopy operators, which reduce to cumulative sums of radial B-spline coefficients, so that the homotopy identities hold exactly. The same operators yield sparse commuting projections that preserve total flux and circulation, and boundary-compatible homotopies that solve the curl--curl problem with a single mass-matrix inversion. In 3D, the tensor product with a periodic 1D complex carries all properties over to stellarator-like solid tori. Numerical experiments confirm optimal projection accuracy and the predicted regularity, show that the regularity conditions suppress the stiff central modes of the curl--curl operator, allowing more than ten times larger time steps than first-order polar spaces, and that compatible high-order regularity is required for convergent guiding-center orbits near the axis of a discrete vacuum field.
item.dc:creator: Ronald A. Remmerswaal

item.title: A scaled TW-PINN framework for soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate approximation of soliton solutions of the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV) equation remains challenging for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) due to localized wave structures, high-order spatial derivatives, nonlinear interactions between solitons, and difficulties in long-time prediction. In this work, we address these challenges using a scaling PINN framework to approximate KdV soliton solutions. The framework transforms the governing equation into a normalized form, approximates its solution using a PINN solver, and reconstructs the solution in the original variables through inverse scaling. We introduce scaling transformations and PINN solvers tailored to one- and two-soliton problems. For the one-soliton case, we employ a PINN solver that incorporates a traveling-wave coordinate to capture soliton propagation. For the two-soliton case, we employ a two-step training procedure for the PINN solver. The first step learns the individual soliton profiles and estimates their propagation speeds, while the second step uses the estimated speeds to construct traveling-wave coordinates in the PINN solver and approximate the full two-soliton solution, including nonlinear interactions. We also introduce soliton-informed sampling (SIS), which places additional collocation points around the soliton trajectories. Numerical results show that the scaling PINN framework accurately captures one-soliton propagation, resolves two-soliton interactions, and preserves soliton profiles during long-time extrapolation in both cases. An additional three-soliton experiment suggests the applicability of the proposed two-step training procedure to multi-soliton solutions.
item.dc:creator: Seungwan Han, Jiaxi Gu, Daniel Olmos-Liceaga, Jae-Hun Jung

item.title: EDP-PI-DOSnet: An Energy Dissipation Preserving Neural Solver for Two-Phase Flow Problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.09430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Preserving the energy dissipation properties of gradient flow equations is important for the stability and reliability of numerical approximations, particularly in long-time simulations. In this paper, we propose a class of energy-dissipation-preserving physics-informed deep operator splitting networks (EDP-PI-DOSnets) for solving gradient flow equations. The proposed framework incorporates classical structure-preserving numerical schemes into neural network architectures, allowing the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws to be preserved. In particular, suitable constraints are imposed on the convolution kernels to ensure that the learned discrete operators are symmetric and negative semidefinite. Furthermore, several network formulations are developed based on the Crank--Nicolson (CN), scalar auxiliary variable Crank--Nicolson (SAV/CN), and relaxed discrete variational derivative (R-DVD-1) schemes. Meanwhile, a physics-informed loss function based on the residuals of the governing equations is employed. Numerical experiments show that the predicted solutions are in good agreement with the reference solutions while satisfying the corresponding discrete energy dissipation laws. The results also suggest stable behavior during long-time recursive prediction and the potential applicability of the proposed framework to two-phase flow problems.
item.dc:creator: Jizu Huang, Yue Qian, Tao Zhou

item.title: Mathematical analysis and vectorized FEM implementation of logarithmic strain space framework for finite strains: a case study on elastoplasticity
item.description: arXiv:2611.09492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the mathematical and computational aspects of the logarithmic strain space framework for finite-strain models in nonlinear continuum mechanics, focusing on the classical von Mises elastoplastic model with linear kinematic hardening. To overcome the lack of coercivity and lower-semicontinuity in the quadratic Hencky energy, we introduce higher-gradient regularization and prove the existence of energetic solutions for rate-independent quasistatic evolution under time-dependent Dirichlet loading. Complementarily, we develop a vectorized MATLAB finite-element implementation of the framework leveraging page-wise matrix functions and operations, and our custom vectorization library. Computational benchmarks show that local tensor operations are significantly accelerated, the logarithmic-strain approach does not substantially increase computational costs, and the implementation robustly handles large rotations and deformations.
item.dc:creator: Miroslav Frost, Martin Kru\v{z}\'{\i}k, Alexej Moskovka, Jan Valdman

item.title: Symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for bounded and unbounded operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.09571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish rigorous local-error bounds for the entire family of symmetric Zassenhaus splittings for possibly unbounded operators, under explicit assumptions on commutator bounds, regularity-preserving flows, and conjugation identities. Truncated symmetric Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansions yield an explicit coefficient formula for the Zassenhaus exponents and identify vanishing commutator expressions. In order to extend these cancellations to the realm of unbounded operators, we prove a general theorem on finite expansions of multiple operator conjugations with controlled integral remainders. For splittings of order 2n, our argument gives the sufficient commutator-length bound 4n-1, revealing regularity requirements that are not apparent from the formal order calculation. Using the Schr\"odinger equation with a quadratic potential as an example, we show that the order-dependent regularity requirements can reduce to one fixed weighted Sobolev space for all splitting orders.
item.dc:creator: Paul Bergold, Arieh Iserles, Karolina Kropielnicka

item.title: Bayesian Inverse Problems for EUV reflectometry with regularized JKO scheme
item.description: arXiv:2611.09574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Bayesian inverse problem in EUV reflectometry, where optical constants and layer thicknesses are inferred from angle- and wavelength-resolved reflection measurements. The physical process is modeled and evaluated using an efficient forward model based on the transfer matrix method. As an alternative to computationally expensive sampling-based inference, we employ an Eulerian, entropically regularized Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler divergence via proximal steps in the Wasserstein space. Using the Benamou--Brenier dynamic formulation and a Hopf-Cole transform, each JKO step is reformulated as a pair of heat equations coupled only through their initial and terminal conditions, enabling an efficient fixed-point solver. The resulting high-dimensional densities are discretized on tensor-product grids and represented in tensor-train format, exploiting Kronecker structure for scalable computation. Preconditioning based on estimated posterior moments further improves tractability. We test the method with numerical experiments on EUV reflectometry data for a ruthenium--silicon ($\ce{Ru}$ on $\ce{Si}$) specimen and compare the learned tensor-train posterior to ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) reference samples. We demonstrate a use case in which we are able to reuse the tensor-train posterior to obtain samples for shifted target distributions with less computational effort than a comparable MCMC method.
item.dc:creator: Vitalii Aksenov, Oliver Henze

item.title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coarse-to-Fine Finite Element Solver for Heterogeneous Darcy Flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.09593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum linear system algorithms offer theoretical potential for solving large sparse systems from PDE discretizations. However, applying them directly to fine-scale problems remains impractical on near-term hardware because of limited qubits, restricted circuit depth, and noise. They also prepare a quantum state rather than solution coefficients, whose recovery requires measurement and reconstruction. In this work, we develop a hybrid quantum-classical coarse-to-fine finite element framework for heterogeneous Darcy flow. We investigate whether a measured quantum coarse solution improves fine-grid initialization and reduces subsequent classical solver work. Rather than solve the full fine-scale system on a quantum device, we apply a method inspired by the Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS) to the Galerkin coarse system. We reconstruct the approximate coarse solution from measurements, prolongate it to the fine grid, and use it to initialize a classical preconditioned iterative solve.} Numerical experiments on steady heterogeneous Darcy flow and a time-dependent SPE10-based problem show that measured quantum coarse solutions can improve fine-grid initialization, while classical correction recovers accurate pressure fields. The effect on classical solver iterations depends on the problem. All quantum computations were simulated using Qiskit Aer.
item.dc:creator: Kapil Chawla, Sanghyun Lee, Jonathan Valyou

item.title: SparseModesNet for coupled thermal-hydraulic-mechanical system in heterogeneous porous media
item.description: arXiv:2611.09616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) models describe interactions among displacement, fluid pressure, and temperature in geothermal systems. Fine-mesh simulations over many time steps are costly, particularly with heterogeneous permeability and thermal conductivity or fracture networks that alter fluid and heat transport. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) reduces the number of unknowns but can require many modes because its reconstruction is linear. We apply SparseModesNet to reconstruct coupled THM solutions using a small set of selected modes and a neural-network nonlinear decoder. Starting from a larger collection of candidate modes, SparseModesNet selects modes to reduce reconstruction error rather than simply retaining those with the highest energy. We compare SparseModesNet with POD on three problems: a two-dimensional heterogeneous medium, a two-dimensional connected fracture network, and a three-dimensional geometry based on Utah FORGE fractures. We evaluate reconstructed displacement, pressure, and temperature fields, as well as pressure- and temperature-based quantities of interest. We also test temporal interpolation by training on a subset of snapshots and reconstructing omitted snapshots within the same time interval. For the same reduced dimension, SparseModesNet achieves smaller reconstruction errors than POD and accurately recovers the solution fields and selected geothermal quantities of interest.
item.dc:creator: Kapil Chawla, Tomoki Koike, Sanghyun Lee, Julie Bessac

item.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization
item.description: arXiv:2611.09706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Manavalan, Carola Bibiane Schoenlieb

item.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.09813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a conforming virtual element framework for differential forms on general polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. Recursive local Hodge-Laplace boundary value problems define a trimmed virtual de Rham complex, from which moment constraints yield a complete subcomplex. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial spaces of differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom and computable polynomial projections. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and both complexes have cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual families, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and mesh-uniform norm equivalences in all form degrees. We further derive canonical interpolation error bounds and discrete Poincar'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge-Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity. Moreover, the two conforming complexes are cochain isomorphic to their fully discrete counterparts (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2025, doi:10.4171/JEMS/1602), and the norm equivalences provide a key analytical bridge between the conforming and fully discrete formulations.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojing Dong, Yibing Han, Yunqing Huang

item.title: Mass-lumped finite elements with maximum-bound preservation and original-energy dissipation for the degenerate-mobility Allen-Cahn equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we propose a mass-lumped finite element method for the Allen-Cahn equation that incorporates nonlinear mobility which may degenerate. The spatial approximation uses continuous, piecewise linear, mass-lumped finite elements, while convex splitting is employed for the double-well potential in time. Under the standard non-obtuse mesh condition, it is shown that the resulting fully discrete method preserves the maximum-bound principle unconditionally: if the initial approximation takes values in $[-1, 1]$, then so does the numerical solution at every time level. Additionally, the method dissipates the original discrete Ginzburg-Landau energy without any time-step restriction, even when the mobility vanishes at pure phases. This analysis relies on the monotonicity of the lumped finite element operator and the convexity of the split potential. Numerical experiments confirm these theoretical properties and demonstrate the robustness of the method in phase-separation dynamics involving degenerate mobility.
item.dc:creator: Himanshu Kumar Dwivedi, Matthias Ehrhardt

item.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
item.description: arXiv:2611.09853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.
item.dc:creator: Salma Raiouadi, Mohamed El Alaoui Talibi, Mouna Hilal

item.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.08490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermal simulation is becoming increasingly critical in modern IC design and manufacturing. Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks. We prove a stopping-time residual identity showing that the expected tail after truncation equals the current attenuation weight multiplied by the temperature at the stopping location. This identity enables a prior-corrected single-point estimator: a cheap, noisy prior replaces the unknown continuation value, making the truncation bias scale with prior error rather than absolute temperature and yielding an error-controlled threshold-selection rule. For multi-point queries, FasterRW further converts cross-query pass-through tails into pseudo-samples and refines the resulting observations in prior-error coordinates through kriging. Compared with prior state-of-the-art methods, FasterRW achieves up to $28\times$ acceleration while maintaining accuracy. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/ShiningSord/FastRW.
item.dc:creator: Zixiao Wang, Tianshu Hou, Chenghan Wang, Zhen Zhuang, Leilei Jin, Tsung-Yi Ho, Farzan Farnia, Bei Yu

item.title: On the (non-)closedness of the set of ReLU networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.09887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the set $\mathcal{N}_N$ of ReLU networks with one hidden layer and at most $N\in\mathbb N$ neurons is weakly closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$, for a bounded connected open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$. Consequently, every coercive, weakly lower semicontinuous energy on this space attains its minimum over $\mathcal{N}_N$. This covers the Deep Ritz method with convex integrands, Sobolev training and Lipschitz learning. Moreover, as the weight decay parameter tends to zero, minimizers of the regularized problem converge, up to subsequences, to minimizers with minimal parameter norm. We also prove that the set of ReLU networks with two hidden layers of bounded widths is not closed in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ or in $C(\overline\Omega)$. This disproves a conjecture of Petersen, Raslan and Voigtlaender.
item.dc:creator: Eloi Martinet, Leon Bungert

item.title: The Finite Difference Method, for the heat equation on Sierpi\'{n}ski simplices
item.description: arXiv:1802.09925v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the sequel, we extend our previous work on the Minkowski Curve to Sierpi\'{n}ski simplices (Gasket and Tetrahedron), in the case of the heat equation. First, we build the finite difference scheme. Then, we give a theoretical study of the error, compute the scheme error, give stability conditions, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Contrary to existing work, we do not call for approximations of the eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Nizare Riane, Claire David

item.title: Automatic Synthesis of Low-Complexity Translation Operators for the Fast Multipole Method
item.description: arXiv:2305.17867v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The FMM is the leading approach for attaining linear complexity in the evaluation of long-range (e.g. Coulomb) many-body interactions. We demonstrate a new, hybrid symbolic-numerical method for the automatic synthesis of all families of translation operators required for the execution of the Fast Multipole Method (FMM). Our method is dimension-independent (demonstrated in 2D and 3D) and applicable to any translation-invariant kernel. Low complexity in translation operators for the FMM is usually achieved by algorithms specialized for a potential obeying a specific partial differential equation (PDE). Absent a PDE or specialized algorithms, Taylor series based FMMs or kernel-independent FMM have been used, at asymptotically higher expense. When symbolically provided with a constant-coefficient elliptic PDE obeyed by the potential, our algorithm can automatically synthesize translation operators requiring $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, where $p$ is the expansion order and $d$ is dimension, compared with $\mathrm{O}(p^{2d})$ operations in a naive approach carried out on (Cartesian) Taylor expansions. This is achieved by using a compression scheme that asymptotically reduces the number of terms in the Taylor expansion and then operating directly on this "compressed" representation. Judicious exploitation of shared subexpressions permits formation, translation, and evaluation of local and multipole expansions to be performed in $\mathrm{O}(p^d)$ operations, while an FFT-based scheme permits multipole-to-local translations in $\mathrm{O}(p^{d-1}\log(p))$ operations. We demonstrate computational scaling of code generation and evaluation as well as numerical accuracy through numerical experiments on a number of potentials from classical physics.
item.dc:creator: Isuru Fernando, Chaoqi Lin, Andreas Kl\"ockner

item.title: A structure and asymptotic preserving scheme for the quasineutral limit of the Vlasov-Poisson system
item.description: arXiv:2504.04826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we propose a new numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system that is both asymptotically consistent and stable in the quasineutral regime, i.e. when the Debye length $\lambda$ is small compared to the characteristic spatial scale of the physical domain. Our approach consists in reformulating the Vlasov-Poisson system as a hyperbolic problem by applying a spectral expansion in the basis of Hermite functions in the velocity space and in designing a structure-preserving scheme for the time and spatial variables. Through this Hermite formulation, we establish a convergence result for the electric field toward its quasineutral limit together with explicit error estimates in $\lambda$. Following this path, we then propose a fully discrete numerical method for the Vlasov-Poisson system, inspired by the approach in arXiv:2306.14605, and rigorously prove that it is uniformly consistent in the quasineutral limit regime. Finally, we present several numerical simulations to illustrate the behavior of the proposed scheme. These results demonstrate the capability of our method to describe quasineutral plasmas, illustrate its stability and confirm its asymptotic preserving property.
item.dc:creator: Alain Blaustein (Centre Inria de l'Universit\'e de Lille), Giacomo Dimarco (Universit\`a di Ferrara), Francis Filbet (Universit\'e de Toulouse), Marie-H\'el\`ene Vignal (Universit\'e de Toulouse)

item.title: Novel technique based on L\'eja Points Approximation for Log-determinant Estimation of Large matrices
item.description: arXiv:2603.02207v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The computation of the Log-determinant of large, sparse, symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices is essential in many scientific computational fields such as numerical linear algebra and machine learning. In low dimensions, Cholesky is preferred, but in high dimensions, its computation may be prohibitive due to memory limitation. To circumvent this, Krylov subspace techniques have proven to be efficient but may be computationally expensive due to the required orthogonalization processes. In this paper, we introduce a Newton-L\'eja interpolation based approach for estimating log-determinants, where the implementation is only based on matrix multiplications and a rough estimation of eigenvalue bounds of the matrix. The method employs an adaptive stopping criterion to select the degree of interpolation according to the data and introduces a centered, scaled-based formulation for computing the logarithmic divided differences. By combining Newton-L\'eja interpolation with a randomized algorithm called Hutch++, we obtain a matrix-free log-determinant estimation framework that avoids explicit matrix factorization and Krylov basis orthogonalization. We establish approximation error bounds for the Newton-L\'eja interpolation and derive an inexact oracle error bound that separates stochastic trace estimation from the approximation errors in the projected and residual components. Numerical experiments on both large sparse synthetic matrices (Gaussian Markov Random fields) and large-scale real-world matrices demonstrate that our method substantially reduces computational time while retaining competitive accuracy, thereby confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and favorable accuracy-cost trade-off for large-scale log-determinant estimation compared with stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ) and related stochastic trace-estimation methods.
item.dc:creator: Verlon Roel Mbingui, Antoine Tambue, Issa Karambal

item.title: Discrete hypocoercive estimates for discontinuous Galerkin methods: application to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system
item.description: arXiv:2603.26218v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop and analyze a class of structure-preserving discontinuous Galerkin schemes for the nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck model, reformulated as a hyperbolic system through a Hermite expansion in the velocity variable. We discretize the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with the discontinuous Galerkin method, while the Poisson equation is approximated with either a discontinuous Galerkin method or a Raviart-Thomas mixed finite element method. We prove the exponential relaxation to equilibrium for suitable initial data, uniformly with respect to the discretization parameters thanks to discrete hypocoercivity arguments. Moreover, we check that the resulting semi-discrete schemes preserve the physical invariants along with the L 2 variational structure of the linearized model. Numerical simulations verify the accuracy and the long-time behavior of the scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yi Cai (USTC), Alain Blaustein (RAPSODI), Tao Xiong (USTC), Francis Filbet (IMT)

item.title: Adaptive refinement based on local approximation power of hierarchical spline spaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.19555v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an adaptive refinement strategy for hierarchical B-splines that increases the approximation power of every marked cell by at least one. Here, the approximation power of a cell is the finest level $\ell$ such that all the B-splines of level $\ell$ that do not vanish on the cell belong to the hierarchical space. This increase can be achieved with the standard refinement of hierarchical meshes, in which each cell is subdivided at most once per step, provided that the regions formed at each level by the cells with this property are nested. We call the hierarchical meshes with this nesting property \emph{weakly admissible}, characterize them, and prove that the proposed refinement preserves weak admissibility. We also prove a complexity estimate: the number of cells created along the adaptive process is bounded by a constant times the total number of marked cells. Moreover, we extend known local $L^q$ estimates for a multilevel quasi-interpolant on these meshes to Sobolev norms, showing that the local error bound on each active cell is governed by its approximation power, which supports using this quantity to drive the refinement. Numerical experiments illustrate the local gain of resolution produced by the proposed strategy, as well as its robustness with respect to the marking criterion and the marking parameter.
item.dc:creator: Gustavo A. Fernandez Lezcano, Eduardo M. Garau, B\'arbara S. Ivaniszyn

item.title: A structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume scheme on vertex-staggered unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2604.21906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a structure-preserving semi-implicit finite volume method on vertex-based staggered meshes for the compatible discretization of first-order systems of time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). The method preserves divergence-free and curl-free vector fields exactly thanks to the compatible vertex-staggered discretization of the state variables on unstructured grids consisting of primal Delaunay triangles and their dual polygons. For the weakly compressible Euler equations, the scheme is asymptotic preserving, yielding a consistent discretization of the incompressible limit as the Mach number goes to zero. The scheme applies to a broad spectrum of PDEs, including the weakly compressible and incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) system, and the incompressible version of the first-order hyperbolic Godunov-Peshkov-Romenski (GPR) model for continuum mechanics. The computational domain is covered by a primal triangular mesh and a dual tessellation made of star polygons. Scalar quantities (pressure, density, viscous stress) are defined at nodes, with pressure updated implicitly in a continuous finite element fashion, yielding a symmetric and positive definite pressure system. Instead, vector fields (velocity, momentum, magnetic and distortion fields) are stored at triangle barycenters and evolved explicitly using a compatible finite volume scheme. With the semi-implicit discretization, the CFL restriction is independent of the sound speed, allowing simulations at low Mach numbers. The compatible formulation ensures an exactly divergence-free velocity field in the incompressible limit, an exactly divergence-free magnetic field for MHD, and an exactly curl-free inverse deformation gradient in solid mechanics. The scheme has been extended to second-order accuracy. The method is validated through a set of test cases.
item.dc:creator: Elena Bernardelli, Elena Gaburro, Michael Dumbser

item.title: Vertex interpolation by bivariate $C^1$ cubic splines: counterexamples, geometric stability, and indecomposable defects
item.description: arXiv:2609.06364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study vertex evaluation on the full space of continuously differentiable piecewise cubic polynomials on a fixed planar triangulation. A complete dual description turns failure of interpolation into balanced edge weights with nonzero vertex loading. It leads to exact counterexamples with 17, 25, 31 and 41 vertices, each with one relation and the classical lower-bound dimension. The 31- and 41-vertex examples have interior graphs that are trees. We give a geometric construction criterion for a sector-completion family and a certified implicit construction outside that family. With all boundary vertices fixed, the nearby bad configurations form a four-dimensional smooth locus in the 17-vertex case, two intersecting components of dimensions six and five in the 25-vertex case, and isolated transverse points in the two tree examples. A common Schur-complement estimate explains their different interpolation costs. We first realize arbitrary defect by decomposable chains of the 41-vertex example. We then construct obstructions from individually interpolatory blocks, prove that the capacity of one complete edge is exactly five, and build a fixed-square family with arbitrarily large strongly indecomposable defect. The latter excludes two triangle-disjoint connected normal bad submeshes even when those submeshes may have holes.
item.dc:creator: Junkai Qiu

item.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34539v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a class of nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Yue Wu, Chi-Wang Shu

item.title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
item.description: arXiv:2611.08169v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a second-order, semi-implicit time-stepping scheme for the shallow-water equations on the sphere discretised with compatible finite elements. The scheme splits the advection operator from the wave operator, applying a DG-upwind SSPRK3 method to the advection part and an $H(\text{div})$-conforming implicit discretisation to the wave part, solved efficiently via hybridisation. The scheme follows a three-step symmetric splitting: an explicit half-step, a full advection step, and an implicit half-step that simultaneously projects the velocity back into the $H(\text{div})$ space. This symmetry guarantees global second-order accuracy and confines the stability restriction to the CFL condition of the advection step alone. The time-step can therefore be extended beyond this limit by subcycling the advection step without additional implicit solves. The method is implemented in Firedrake and validated against a standard suite of spherical shallow-water benchmarks, demonstrating stable results for Courant numbers up to 1 (with two advection subcycles) with second-order finite elements, second-order convergence, and good parallel scaling.
item.dc:creator: Karina Kowalczyk, Colin Cotter

item.title: Quantitative Universal Approximation for Noisy Quantum Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2604.02064v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a quantitative universal approximation theorem for noisy quantum neural networks (QNNs), with explicit non-asymptotic error bounds in terms of the number of accuracy blocks, the qubit count, the number of two-qubit gates, and hardware noise parameters. Motivated by quantitative finance, where target functions are expectations of payoffs, we first extend existing noiseless bounds to expectation functions and derive explicit constants for exponential Levy models, covering the Black-Scholes price of (truncated) European Put options. We then formulate the noisy circuit via quantum channels, obtain a fidelity-based bound for general noise models, and specialise to depolarising noise with readout error, calibrated to real hardware. Finally, we provide a detailed numerical analysis for option pricing in the Black-Scholes model, testing our results on actual noisy quantum hardware.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Gonon, Antoine Jacquier, Marcel Mordarski

item.title: DeepRitzSplit: A Variational Neural Operator Framework for Gradient Flows with Application to Dendritic Growth
item.description: arXiv:2604.18261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Phase-field models are widely used to simulate microstructure evolution but their numerical solution remains computationally demanding. Neural operator surrogates provide a promising alternative, yet existing approaches are data-driven, requiring large datasets and exhibiting limited robustness when extrapolating to unseen configurations. We introduce DeepRitzSplit, an unsupervised neural operator framework for gradient-flow systems based on a variational formulation of energy-stable splitting schemes. It learns the time evolution semigroup associated with a convex-concave free-energy decomposition by minimizing the underlying variational problem at each time step. It is designed to inherit the dissipative structure of the underlying gradient flow without requiring trajectory datasets. We further introduce a Reaction-Diffusion Neural Operator (RDNO) architecture motivated by splitting schemes, with separate reaction and diffusion components to improve training efficiency and interpretability. We assess the approach on the Allen-Cahn equation and apply it to a phase-field model of anisotropic dendritic growth during solidification. In the Allen-Cahn benchmark, DeepRitzSplit shows better generalization than the supervised baseline on the out-of-distribution configurations tested, using 180 training configurations. In dendritic growth, the method captures the overall phase morphology and dendrite tip velocity well, while the tip radius is more sensitive to the training strategy. Refinement based on the residual of the splitting scheme markedly improves this second-order morphological quantity. The trained operators retain good predictive capabilities on configurations substantially different from the training set. These results demonstrate the potential of variationally trained neural operators as physically informed surrogates for accelerated microstructure simulations.
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Appolaire, Ludovick Gagnon, Chih-Kang Huang, Miha Zalo\v{z}nik
